title: July NFP Falls 23,000, May-June Revised Down 103,000 Combined — S&P 500 Hits Record Close as Fed Hike Odds Tumble
detail: BLS reported nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 in July, far short of the roughly 83,000 gain expected, while May and June payrolls were revised down by a combined 103,000. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1% from 4.2%, largely on a further decline in labor-force participation. Rather than sparking a selloff, markets rallied on reduced hike risk: the S&P 500 closed at a record 7,757.64 (+0.62%), the Dow rose 0.28% to 54,036.93, and the Nasdaq gained 1.3% to 26,690.62. The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 7 basis points to roughly 4.6%. Fed funds futures showed the odds of a September rate hike — which had surged to roughly 82% after the July 23 oil shock — collapsing after the report, a sharp reversal of the hawkish repricing seen two weeks earlier.

title: China's July Exports Jump 23.9% YoY on AI-Tech Demand and Front-Loading Ahead of New Tariffs
detail: China's exports rose 23.9% year-on-year to $397.85 billion in July, beating the 22.2% forecast though easing from June's 27.0% pace, driven by strong AI-related tech demand (semiconductor export value nearly doubled YoY, overall high-tech exports up 40.7%) and manufacturers rushing shipments to the US ahead of the new Section 301 tariffs that replaced the lapsed 10% levy with a 12.5% rate in late July. Imports rose 27.7% YoY to $285.35 billion, easing from June's 36% jump, leaving the trade surplus at $112.5 billion, above the $107 billion forecast.
